analysis:
Examined ci.yml metadata, the complete supplied patch, and BASE lines 1–827 against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041. HEAD lines 43–47 replace one five-runner provider lane with five one-runner lanes; line 143 selects the lane using the numeric matrix shard. Names match the unchanged five-shard matrix (BASE 141–142), and the total requested Mac count remains five. This permits mixed Sandbox/fallback execution rather than whole-group fallback. No permission, secret, checkout, test-admission, timeout, artifact, cache-key or provider-runtime change is shown. The summary still audits executed suites (BASE 364–370), and the final gate still requires both matrix and summary success (763–783). No supported regression to prompt encryption, cache isolation (T-041), attestation/qualification (T-053/T-054), owner-account protection or billing was identified in this scope; CI success is not live serving qualification.
Integration should verify .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and its routing implementation accept the new lane keys, independently reserve runners without cross-shard assignment collisions, and return usable routes for partial Sandbox grants. That implementation is not supplied, so allocation/isolation behavior cannot be established here. Review corresponding routing/workflow tests for the five-key contract. Existing Sandbox use is visible in BASE and is not itself a new vulnerability. Unchanged actions and callers were not examined; this is a local source review, not an audit of runner infrastructure.
